item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The state of siege in Nord-Kivu and Ituri was extended more than 50 times by the government without meaningful public debate about the legality or merits of those extensions.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.4","4B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The extensions and their assessment were documented during 2023, within the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the repeated extensions to the government under President Félix Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Amnesty International is the reporting organization and characterizes the extensions as unlawful; the source does not provide the government's response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Under the state of siege, military authorities appointed by President Tshisekedi used their powers to harass and jail journalists, kill human rights defenders and political activists, and conduct mass pre-trial detention of people considered threats, including people criticizing the state of siege and military authorities.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source describes practices documented during the two-year state of siege and reported in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly links the military authorities to President Tshisekedi's appointments and attributes the state-of-siege framework to his administration.","limitations":["The source does not quantify all alleged incidents or establish individual responsibility for each reported abuse."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"President Tshisekedi's state of siege transferred civilian administration in Nord-Kivu and Ituri to army and police officers, replacing elected governors and suspending elected provincial assemblies; military courts were ordered to prosecute civilians.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.1","4B.2","4B.4"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The arrangement remained in force during 2023 after being imposed in May 2021.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes enforcement of the state of siege and these institutional changes to President Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source does not describe the full legal text of each implementing order or the extent of parliamentary involvement in each extension."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Despite the state of siege's stated goals of improving civilian protection, curbing armed groups, and restoring state authority, attacks against civilians and civilian casualties increased, and the army repeatedly failed to prevent or respond to armed-group attacks.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","8B.1","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source evaluates security trends over the state of siege through the 2023 reporting date.","ruler_attribution":"The stated objectives and continuation of the policy are attributed to President Tshisekedi's government.","limitations":["The source relies on reported information and does not provide a complete counterfactual assessment of what would have occurred without the state of siege."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The UN Joint Human Rights Office reported that the DRC army committed numerous serious human rights violations against civilians during the state of siege.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding concerned the state-of-siege period and was cited in the 2023 source.","ruler_attribution":"The source places the army within the state-of-siege security structure established and maintained by Tshisekedi's administration.","limitations":["This source does not specify the incidents, perpetrators, or disciplinary outcomes for the reported violations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The deteriorating security situation in eastern DRC resulted in more than 4,000 civilian deaths and more than two million forcibly displaced people since 2021, according to figures from the UN and the Kivu Security Tracker.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures cover the period beginning in 2021 and were reported in May 2023, overlapping the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The source presents these outcomes in the context of the state of siege maintained by President Tshisekedi's government.","limitations":["The figures cover a multi-year period and are not limited to events occurring solely in 2023; the source does not assign all deaths or displacement directly to government policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-34b3eac040af6ecf","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The DRC authorities had not complied with the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights requirement to notify the UN Secretary-General in writing and explain circumstances justifying derogations from certain rights during the state of siege.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.2","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The non-compliance was reported while the state of siege remained active in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the failure to the DRC authorities under President Tshisekedi's administration.","limitations":["The source does not identify the specific official responsible for the missing notification or describe any subsequent corrective action."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The source is an Amnesty International press release and primarily reports institutional and human-rights findings; it provides limited evidence about economic policy, social services, nuclear risk, personal integrity, or the ruler's broader 2023 program."]}
